determination_note: READ THIS BEFORE READING THE DETERMINATION. Registered full-span (2022-2025): NOT-YET. ISO tier (2023-2025, rule 30(c)): CALIBRATED — RESTORED 2026-09-13 by session nyiso-233, which LANDED the shared-scorer repair nyiso-232 proved and was not authorized to fix. C1 PASS, C2 PASS, C3a PASS, C3b PASS, C4 PASS, C6 PASS, C8 PASS, with C3c the LONE failing criterion and therefore a ledgered ACCEPTED MODEL-CLASS LIMITATION under rule 22 [R-C3C] — non-downgrading since rubric v3.3, so the ISO tier reads CALIBRATED. Per-year: 2022 NOT-YET, 2023 CALIBRATED, 2024 CALIBRATED, 2025 CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS. WHAT CHANGED, AND WHAT DID NOT: no solve, no re-key, no config field, no offer curve, NOTHING about this keeper's recipe or its dispatch. The run is re-scored because THE SCORER CHANGED — scripts/legitimacy_diagnostics.py::aggregate_floors_by_plant now weights the D-2 plant-class vote by CAPACITY (pmax) instead of by LP ROW COUNT. Row count is a property of the offer curve's band structure, not of the plant, so this keeper's declared, pre-registered ST_GAS smoothing-ladder collapse (88 -> 44 rows) moved whole sites between class denominators: Ravenswood (plant 2500) carries 1724.8 MW of ST_GAS against 268.5 MW of CC_REGULAR — 6.4:1 — yet its rows read 4 vs 7, so an 87%-steam site was labelled CC_REGULAR and its dispatch counted against the wrong denominator. MEASURED IN A CONTROLLED A/B (identical inputs, only the weight differs): every NUMERATOR is bit-identical to 4 dp in all 20 rows — forced energy 1.9187 / 1.9955 / 2.3764 / 2.2003 TWh, unchanged — while ST_GAS's denominator moves 5.7046 -> 9.2318, 5.8134 -> 13.4962, 6.4861 -> 11.5421, 7.7309 -> 12.1256 TWh, so the forced share reads 20.78 / 14.79 / 20.59 / 18.15 % against the 30 % cap instead of 33.63 / 34.33 / 36.64 / 28.46 %. Three FAIL->pass flips (2022/2023/2024). All four are BELOW the superseded nyiso-231 keeper's 23.1 / 16.5 / 21.4 / 19.0 %, which is what physics demands: the same floors are a smaller share of a class that now runs more. THE PASS IS NOT VACUOUS — ST_GAS is MATERIAL on both arms (load share 11.2-13.1 % before, 15.9-18.8 % after, against the rule-20 2 % floor), so it did not pass by being reclassified as too small to gate. C8 failing was ALSO what stripped C3c of lone-failure status under rule 22 guard (a); with C8 passing, C3c reverts to the ledgered caveat it is everywhere else. AUTHORISATION: a shared scorer reaches every ISO column, which rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE] forbids a NYISO lane from deciding alone — landed on the OWNER'S EXPLICIT RULING in session nyiso-233 to measure every ISO and then land it, with the disposition that a verdict change elsewhere is a CORRECTION, not a regression. MEASURED CROSS-ISO, 10 bundle-years / 3 ISOs / 11,328 floor rows: CAISO byte-identical on every row (0 flips); SPP denominators move (COAL 68.83 -> 72.44 TWh in 2023) but ZERO verdict changes; NYISO is the only ISO whose verdict moves. ERCOT / PJM / MISO / NEISO carry no committed floors npz and are UNMEASURED, not shown to be clean. The four pre-registered stop conditions all cleared (S1 0 zero-capacity plants, S2 0 labels lost to '', S3 11,328/11,328 rows backfilled, S4 blast radius confined to D-2/D-4). STILL GENUINELY FAILING, NOT ABSORBED: 2022 C3a at -11.6 % (pre-registered as the accepted cost of the nyiso-232 arming), 2022 C1 CC_REGULAR +5.07 TWh / +3.8 pp, and 2022 C3b NRMSE 0.218 — these are what keep the FOUR-YEAR bundle at NOT-YET, and under rule 30(c) a held-out year neither certifies nor decertifies the ISO. C3c is reported at full magnitude and is NOT a pass: model 7 / 0 / 0 / 4 h above $300 against 101 / 10 / 13 / 42 h actual. The D-4 provenance failures are PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by the repair (9 unit-conduct rows, IDENTICAL failure set on both vote bases). Records: docs/FINDING-nyiso233-d2-capacity-weighted-vote-2026-09-13.md, results/calibration/PRECOMMIT-nyiso233-d2-capacity-weighted-vote.md, scripts/probes/_nyiso233_d2_capacity_vote_measure.py.
